tools.label: ESLint
tools.why: nothing checks the frontend sources, so a wrong import is found by the build or not at all
tools.legacyWhy: ESLint 9 reads the flat config only; the eslintrc form, an .eslintrc file or the eslintConfig key in package.json, is ignored unless the run is pinned to ESLint 8

tools.label: Stylelint
tools.why: stylesheets are unchecked, and a mistake in CSS fails silently instead of loudly

tools.label: Psalm
tools.why: the PHP side has no static analysis, which is what catches a wrong type before the server does

tools.label: PHPUnit
tools.why: there is no test harness in the checkout, so nothing can be run against a change

tools.label: PHP-CS-Fixer
tools.why: no coding standard is applied to the PHP sources, so formatting is settled in review instead of by a command

tools.label: REUSE
tools.why: licensing is not machine-checkable, which the App Store and every distribution ask for

tools.label: EditorConfig
tools.why: indentation is whatever each contributor's editor does

lines: Version drift: appinfo/info.xml says 0.1.0, package.json says 0.0.1, package-lock.json says 0.0.1, package-lock.json packages[""] says 0.0.1.

make version of ncmake bumps info.xml, composer.json and package.json and re-syncs package-lock.json in one step, so they cannot drift apart. ncmake's lint-version workflow fails a push or a pull request on exactly this drift. The App Store and the server read info.xml, npm and composer read their own manifest. Whichever is behind, a release ends up carrying more than one version number, and only one of them reaches the user.
appinfo/info.xml states no <repository> and no <bugs>.

<repository> is the only machine-readable link from a published release back to the source it was built from, and <bugs> is where the App Store page sends a report. Without them a user of the release has no way back to the project.
<website> is not set either.
engines.node ^18 || ^20 in package.json admits only end-of-life Node lines: the release is built on Node 20, which reached end of life on 2026-04-30.
That Node receives no security fixes, and the lockfile is resolved for it. The oldest line still maintained is Node 22.
Node release dates from schedule.json of nodejs/Release, as of 2026-11-13.
The app id is integration_stickers, the checkout directory is nextcloud_stickerpicker.

The server finds an app by its directory name, so the installed directory has to be named after the id. A checkout can be named anything, which is why this is a note and not a defect - but a tarball built from this directory name would not load.
Declares Nextcloud 32 to 34; the oldest maintained major is 33 (the Maintenance and Release Schedule of nextcloud/server), the newest released 35 (the release tags of nextcloud/server).
min-version 32 reaches below the oldest maintained major (33), which means the code has to keep working with APIs that are no longer tested upstream.
Node stated as ^18 || ^20 (package.json engines.node).
Not stated in .nvmrc, so nothing keeps the other places from drifting away from it.
Tooling in the checkout: ESLint (.eslintrc.cjs, superseded form).

ESLint is configured in .eslintrc.cjs: ESLint 9 reads the flat config only; the eslintrc form, an .eslintrc file or the eslintConfig key in package.json, is ignored unless the run is pinned to ESLint 8.
No Stylelint configuration: stylesheets are unchecked, and a mistake in CSS fails silently instead of loudly.
No Psalm configuration: the PHP side has no static analysis, which is what catches a wrong type before the server does.
No PHPUnit configuration: there is no test harness in the checkout, so nothing can be run against a change.
No PHP-CS-Fixer configuration: no coding standard is applied to the PHP sources, so formatting is settled in review instead of by a command.
No REUSE configuration: licensing is not machine-checkable, which the App Store and every distribution ask for.
No EditorConfig configuration: indentation is whatever each contributor's editor does.
package.json declares the script lint, which no installed workflow runs.
The template lint-eslint of nextcloud/.github runs lint: make workflows-install W=lint-eslint
A check that no workflow runs on a pull request catches only what the contributor who remembers to run it catches.
Licence agpl (appinfo/info.xml), AGPL-3.0-or-later (composer.json).
agpl in appinfo/info.xml is a deprecated App Store value, shown there as AGPLv3+, which is AGPL-3.0-or-later. With min-version 32 info.xml can state an SPDX id instead.
No LICENSES/ directory, so the licence text itself is not in the checkout, which is what REUSE and the distributions check for.
PHP 8.1 is the floor in appinfo/info.xml and in composer.json, platform 8.1.0.
package-lock.json (lockfileVersion 3) in the checkout.
The ncmake bootstrap stub is in place (21 lines).
Every directory the shipped PHP reaches through __DIR__ and the frontend through linkTo is in the shipped file set.
All 11 declared packages are named somewhere in the checkout, 1 of them by convention.
